context.note: Items marked merged are in the master branch only. They are not in a release until a release containing them is published.
context.release_note: v31.2, v30.4 and v29.5 published the same day. v32.0 was tagged 2026-10-21 but never released. v31.3 and v30.5 were tagged 2026-11-17 with no published release as of 2026-11-18.

status_scale.discussion: talked about on a list or forum, no concrete proposal
status_scale.proposal: written proposal (BIP draft, design doc, PR description) not yet merged
status_scale.merged: merged into a project's main branch, not yet released
status_scale.released: shipped in a tagged release of that software
status_scale.documentation: specification or documentation change only; no software behavior changes
status_scale.backport_merged: merged into a maintenance branch; tagged release inclusion is not established by the merge

items.title: Bitcoin Core 32.1 released as the new major version (32.0 was tagged but never released)
items.what_happened: Bitcoin Core 32.1 was published on 2026-10-28. Its release notes state that 32.0, although tagged, was never fully announced or released due to last-minute issues, so 32.1 is the first release of the 32.x series.
items.why_it_matters: Notable changes per the release notes include default -maxconnections raised from 125 to 200 with a new -inboundrelaypercent option, a global transaction-relay rate limit (-txsendrate), a new mempool-based fee estimator combined into estimatesmartfee, PSBT v2 as the default for PSBT-creating RPCs, a custom HTTP server replacing libevent, a smaller txindex, and a fix for a -walletnotify command-injection issue via crafted wallet names. With this release, 29.x and older are End of Life.
items.not_yet: Release notes say medium/high severity vulnerability disclosures (stated as 3, fixed in 30.0) are scheduled for about two weeks after release; those disclosures are not covered here.

items.title: Bitcoin Core 31.2 maintenance release
items.what_happened: Bitcoin Core 31.2 was published on 2026-10-28 with bug fixes and backports.
items.why_it_matters: It brings BIP 323 handling (version bits 5-28 ignored for soft-fork signaling warnings), a 10,000-entry cap on the private-broadcast queue, chainstate compaction, a timeout for peers whose send buffer stays paused, and Tor/network fixes to the 31.x line.
items.not_yet: none

items.title: Bitcoin Core 30.4 maintenance release
items.what_happened: Bitcoin Core 30.4 was published on 2026-10-28 with a small set of backports.
items.why_it_matters: Includes BIP 323 version-bit handling, assuming v2 transport for addresses from DNS seeds, and the paused-send-peer timeout.
items.not_yet: none

items.title: Bitcoin Core 29.5 released; 29.x now End of Life
items.what_happened: Bitcoin Core 29.5 was published on 2026-10-28 with network and build backports.
items.why_it_matters: The 32.1 release notes state that with the new major version, 29.x and older are End of Life and will no longer receive updates, so 29.x users should plan to upgrade.
items.not_yet: none

items.title: 31.3 and 30.5 prepared with a backport of 'process unique tx INVs only'
items.what_happened: Backport PRs merged into the 31.x and 30.x branches pull in #35878 (only process unique transaction INV announcements) and prepare versions 31.3 and 30.5; git tags v31.3 and v30.5 were created on 2026-11-17.
items.why_it_matters: Indicates new maintenance releases are imminent. #35878 avoids processing conflicting transaction announcements that cannot both be accepted.
items.not_yet: No published GitHub release for v31.3 or v30.5 as of 2026-11-18.
items.uncertainty: author-reported: #35878 states there should be no change in observable behavior; the reason for backporting it is not stated in the backport PRs.
items.status_note: Tags exist (2026-11-17) but no release has been published; do not treat as released.

items.title: -maxconnections capped at 2,000 to avoid an orphanage crash
items.what_happened: Values of -maxconnections above 2,000 are now clamped with a warning. The PR merged to master on 2026-10-21, was backported to 32.x, and is listed in the 32.1 release notes.
items.why_it_matters: The PR states the orphanage can abort when more than 3,000 peers have orphan announcements; the cap removes that crash path for operators using very high connection counts.
items.not_yet: none

items.title: Peers that never drain a paused send buffer are now disconnected after 20 minutes
items.what_happened: A peer whose send buffer stays paused (not drained below the 1MB threshold) is now disconnected after a 20-minute timeout. Merged to master 2026-10-26 and listed in the 31.2, 30.4 and 29.5 release notes.
items.why_it_matters: Frees connection slots held by extremely slow or stalled peers.
items.not_yet: Not listed in the 32.1 release notes; on 32.x it is not established to be in a release.

items.title: -acceptnonstdtxn=1 now also admits non-standard scripts on test networks
items.what_happened: On test networks, -acceptnonstdtxn=1 now also skips non-mandatory script checks, allowing transactions that use e.g. OP_NOPx or OP_SUCCESS into the mempool.
items.why_it_matters: Makes it easier to experiment with upgrade-hook opcodes (e.g. covenant or soft-fork prototypes) on test nets without custom builds. Mainnet policy is unchanged.
items.not_yet: In master only; not in a release.

items.title: -persistmempoolv1 option removed
items.what_happened: The temporary -persistmempoolv1 option, which wrote mempool.dat in the old non-obfuscated format for downgrades to v26 and earlier, was removed. Reading v1 files is still supported.
items.why_it_matters: Configurations that set this option will need updating; downgrade to unmaintained v26-and-older with a persisted mempool is no longer supported.
items.not_yet: In master only; not in a release.

items.title: removeprunedfunds RPC deleted
items.what_happened: The removeprunedfunds wallet RPC, deprecated in v32, was removed from master.
items.why_it_matters: Scripts that still call removeprunedfunds (even with -deprecatedrpc) will fail on the next major version.
items.not_yet: In master only; not in a release.

items.title: Wallet RPC options get documented snake_case aliases; camelCase confTarget deprecation scheduled
items.what_happened: snake_case aliases for wallet funding options and listunspent options were added to the CLI, docs and schema; supplying both spellings is rejected; subtract_fee_from_outputs is no longer silently ignored. Separately, deprecation of the mixed-case confTarget option was scheduled for the next cycle.
items.why_it_matters: Fixes a case where a documented-looking option was silently ignored, and signals future removal of camelCase option names that integrators should migrate away from.
items.not_yet: In master only; not in a release. The camelCase removal itself has not happened.

items.title: sendall now rejects unknown options and duplicate inputs
items.what_happened: sendall now errors on unknown keys in its options object and on duplicated entries in inputs.
items.why_it_matters: Per the PRs, a misspelled key could previously spend all UTXOs or broadcast a transaction the caller asked not to broadcast, and a duplicated input double-counted value and produced an invalid transaction that left the wallet in a confusing state until abandoned.
items.not_yet: In master only; not in a release.

items.title: listtransactions crash from integer overflow fixed
items.what_happened: listtransactions now parses count and skip as unsigned 32-bit values and sums them in 64 bits.
items.why_it_matters: Per the PR, a large count+skip previously overflowed and crashed the node; it is reachable by an authenticated RPC caller.
items.not_yet: In master only; not in a release.

items.title: Tor control replies and cached onion keys are now validated
items.what_happened: The node now validates the onion service ID and private key returned by Tor's control port, and validates cached keys before reuse.
items.why_it_matters: The PR describes a command-injection path into ADD_ONION via a malicious key value returned by an impersonated or compromised Tor control endpoint, including by an unprivileged local process under certain timing conditions.
affects: node operators using automatic Tor onion services
items.not_yet: In master only; not in a release.
items.uncertainty: author-reported: the attack scenario and its preconditions are described by the PR author; no advisory or severity rating is linked.
items.status_note: Security hardening in master only; no backport or release established.

items.title: Node ignores a privacy-network peer's view of its address (fingerprint fix)
items.what_happened: When processing a VERSION message from a Tor/I2P peer, the node now ignores the peer-reported addrMe field.
items.why_it_matters: Per the PR, this closes a fingerprint that could help correlate a node's clearnet and privacy-network identities under fairly hard preconditions.
affects: nodes running on both clearnet and Tor/I2P
items.not_yet: In master only; not in a release.
items.uncertainty: author-reported: the fingerprint and its preconditions are described by the PR author.
items.status_note: Privacy fix in master only; no backport or release established.

items.title: Misbehaving peer disconnect no longer drops every peer sharing its IP
items.what_happened: Discouraging a misbehaving peer now disconnects only that connection rather than every connection from the same IP address.
items.why_it_matters: Per the PR, an attacker sharing a Tor exit node with honest clearnet-over-Tor inbound peers could otherwise get all of them disconnected by sending one invalid message.
items.not_yet: In master only; not in a release.
items.uncertainty: author-reported: the attack scenario is the PR author's description.
items.status_note: Merged on the last day of the window; master only.

items.title: Orphan transactions are reconsidered one per message-processing turn
items.what_happened: Instead of validating all of an assigned peer's reconsiderable orphans in one turn, the node now processes a single orphan per turn.
items.why_it_matters: Reduces latency imposed on other peers' message processing when one peer's orphans need re-evaluation.
items.not_yet: In master only; not in a release.

items.title: Block-file flush failures now stop chainstate metadata from advancing
items.what_happened: If flushing block or undo data fails, FlushStateToDisk now returns the error before writing block-index metadata and coins data, and ConnectTip/DisconnectTip propagate it.
items.why_it_matters: Prevents on-disk metadata from referring to block data that was never made durable (for example with a separate, failing -blocksdir), reducing corruption risk after disk errors.
items.not_yet: In master only; not in a release.
items.uncertainty: Classified as tooling for lack of a node-storage category: this is validation/storage robustness and does not change consensus rules.

items.title: BIP460 draft merged: cross-input signature aggregation for a new witness version 2
items.what_happened: BIP460 was merged as a draft. It proposes witness version 2 with Taproot-style key-path spends where inputs can opt into half-aggregation or full-aggregation of signatures across a transaction.
items.why_it_matters: Cross-input signature aggregation could reduce transaction size and fees, especially for many-input transactions such as consolidations and coinjoins. This is a proposed soft fork.
items.not_yet: Draft BIP only; no implementation merged in Bitcoin Core, no activation mechanism, no deployment.

items.title: BIP458 (half-aggregation) and BIP459 (DahLIAS full aggregation) signature schemes merged as drafts
items.what_happened: Two cryptographic BIPs were merged as drafts: BIP458 for non-interactive half-aggregation of BIP340 signatures, and BIP459 for the DahLIAS interactive full-aggregation scheme yielding a constant 64-byte signature.
items.why_it_matters: These are the signature-scheme building blocks referenced by BIP460's cross-input aggregation proposal.
items.not_yet: Draft specifications only; no consensus use.

items.title: BIP139 wallet metadata backup format merged as draft
items.what_happened: BIP139 was added, defining a backup format for wallet metadata with a field registry.
items.why_it_matters: A common format could let wallets export and restore labels and other metadata beyond seeds and descriptors across software.
items.not_yet: Draft only; no known implementation established by the PR.

items.title: BIP394 documents the rawtr() output script descriptor
items.what_happened: BIP394 was added to specify the rawtr() descriptor expression, which Bitcoin Core has implemented since 24.0 without a BIP; BIP380 was updated to reference it.
items.why_it_matters: Closes a specification gap that, per the PR, has led other descriptor libraries to skip or mislabel rawtr().
items.not_yet: Draft BIP; no change to Bitcoin Core behavior.

items.title: BIP379 (Miniscript) advanced to Deployed
items.what_happened: BIP379's status was changed from Draft to Deployed, citing Miniscript support released in Bitcoin Core v26 and other implementations. Test vectors from rust-miniscript were also added.
items.why_it_matters: Formal status change signals the Miniscript spec is considered stable and in use.
items.not_yet: Status change only.

items.title: BIP95 Testnet 5: genesis parameters added, genesis structure and port changed
items.what_happened: BIP95 received the Testnet 5 genesis block parameters, a revised genesis structure (anti-pre-mine commitment in pszTimestamp, OP_RETURN output) and a new default P2P port 18353.
items.why_it_matters: Moves the proposed replacement test network toward being usable; developers and infrastructure providers should note the port and genesis.
items.not_yet: The Bitcoin Core implementation (bitcoin/bitcoin#35861) is still open; Testnet 5 is not in any Bitcoin Core release.
items.status_note: Spec edits to a draft BIP; Core PR open.

items.title: BIP322 upgradeable rules now name Taproot upgrade hooks (v2.1.0)
items.what_happened: BIP322 now treats signatures using an unknown leaf version, the annex, OP_SUCCESSx or an unknown public key type as inconclusive rather than valid.
items.why_it_matters: Per the PR, verifiers following the old text could call such message signatures valid, and implementations disagreed on the annex case.
items.not_yet: Spec change only; implementations must update separately.

items.title: lnd 0.21.6 and 0.20.7 disable MPTCP listeners to mitigate a Linux kernel exploit path
items.what_happened: lnd v0.21.6-beta and v0.20.7-beta (2026-10-30) stop opening Multipath TCP listeners by default; the release notes tie this to a Linux kernel use-after-free (CVE-2026-98432) whose demonstrated remote exploit requires an MPTCP listener, which Go 1.24+ enables by default.
items.why_it_matters: Linux lnd nodes exposed peer/gRPC/REST ports via MPTCP. The notes instruct operators to upgrade, disable MPTCP host-wide, and install a patched kernel; disabling MPTCP is a mitigation, not a fix for the kernel bug.
items.not_yet: The underlying kernel bug is fixed only by a patched kernel; Windows and macOS are stated to be unaffected.
items.uncertainty: CVE-2026-98432 is listed in NVD (published 2026-10-15); details as stated by lnd's release notes.

items.title: lnd 0.21.5 / 0.20.6 enforce a 253 sat/kw commitment fee floor and fix several bugs
items.what_happened: lnd v0.21.5-beta and v0.20.6-beta (2026-10-27) stop proposing or accepting commitment fee rates below 253 sat/kw, reject open_channel below that floor, tighten auxiliary HTLC signature checks on taproot overlay channels, clamp external fee API estimates, and fix a SQLite connection-pool deadlock.
items.why_it_matters: Channels opened below the floor could not carry HTLCs. Older lnd nodes with max-commit-fee-rate-anchors=1 cannot open anchor or taproot channels to upgraded nodes until they change that setting.
items.not_yet: none
items.uncertainty: The taproot overlay check can force close channels with peers running lnd without an aux signer; see release notes.

items.title: lnd 0.21.8 / 0.20.8: batch of correctness fixes for sweeping, channel state and reconnects
items.what_happened: lnd v0.21.8-beta and v0.20.8-beta (2026-11-11) fix low-level bugs across wire decoding, sweeper, channel persistence and gossip; reject duplicate peer channel aliases; preserve funding batch state after publish errors; recover settled AMP HTLCs on-chain; and send channel_reestablish for unconfirmed channels on reconnect.
items.why_it_matters: Several fixes affect fund recovery and channel availability. Operator-visible changes: etcd transactions now fail when an internal read fails, and channels negotiating a zero CSV delay are rejected.
items.not_yet: none
items.uncertainty: Release notes state the v0.21.7-beta tag is the same build; v0.21.8 corrects release metadata and notes.

items.title: lnd backports MPP/AMP HTLC expiry revalidation at set completion
items.what_happened: A fix that re-checks the expiry of every accepted HTLC in a multi-part or AMP payment set when the set completes was backported to the v0.21.x and v0.20.x branches on 2026-11-12, after the 0.21.8/0.20.8 releases.
items.why_it_matters: Previously only the final shard was checked, so earlier shards could fall below the required CLTV margin while waiting for the set to complete.
items.not_yet: Not in a tagged release as of 2026-11-18.

items.title: Core Lightning 26.06.10 ships security fixes across dual funding, splicing, gossip and runes
items.what_happened: Core Lightning v26.06.10 (2026-11-04) is a point release with fixes for responsibly reported vulnerabilities in dual funding and splicing (including tx_signatures signature checks), onchaind HTLC resolution, gossip resource limits, connectd, runes/commando, plugin hooks and hsmd. Tests for the security fixes are temporarily withheld.
items.why_it_matters: Maintainers strongly recommend upgrading. Operator-visible changes include refusing peer dust limits above 5000 sat and tighter zero-conf handling for v2 opens; the notes also recommend binding and rotating runes.
items.not_yet: Technical details of the vulnerabilities have not been published.
items.uncertainty: Severity of individual issues is not stated.

items.title: Core Lightning v26.12 release candidate 1 published
items.what_happened: Core Lightning published v26.12rc1 on 2026-11-18; v26.09 was skipped to handle vulnerability reports. Highlights include deprecating pay in favor of xpay in v27.03, HTLC recovery in lightning-hsmtool, a frozen gRPC wire format, and experimental option_simple_close.
items.why_it_matters: Breaking API changes for developers (cln-rpc required fields, removed notification fields, deprecated runes commands) should be tested before the final release.
items.not_yet: Release candidate only; final v26.12 not released.

items.title: Eclair 0.14.4: security hardening and API now rejects browser requests
items.what_happened: Eclair v0.14.4 (2026-10-15) is a security hardening patch release; its API now rejects requests carrying an Origin header.
items.why_it_matters: Closes a cross-site request forgery path where a web page visited by the operator could trigger authenticated API calls. Web front-ends calling the API directly will break.
items.not_yet: none
items.uncertainty: Details of the other hardening fixes are not itemized in the release notes.

items.title: Eclair 0.14.5 and 0.14.6: more security fixes; splices require confirmed inputs by default
items.what_happened: Eclair v0.14.5 (2026-10-20) and v0.14.6 (2026-10-27) are security hardening patch releases. v0.14.6 adds require-confirmed-inputs-for-splicing (default true) and warns against zero_fee_commitments when splicing with untrusted peers.
items.why_it_matters: Maintainers state some issues can be exploited by malicious nodes. Spending unconfirmed peer inputs in splices could let a peer invalidate the splice and put HTLCs at risk.
items.not_yet: Vulnerability details are not published in the release notes.
items.uncertainty: Severity of individual issues is not stated.

items.title: LDK 0.2.8 fixes counterparty-triggerable bugs including invalid co-op close broadcasts
items.what_happened: LDK v0.2.8 was tagged on 2026-11-11 (CHANGELOG dated Nov 10). Fixes include preventing a malicious counterparty from causing an invalid cooperative close broadcast, avoiding claims of already-spent HTLC outputs, preventing a malicious BOLT 11 invoice from removing a public channel from the graph, and stricter gossip-validation and per-peer queue limits.
items.why_it_matters: Applications built on LDK should update; one fix addresses delays in handling OpenChannelRequest that the changelog says could at worst lead to funds loss.
items.not_yet: 0.3 is still in release candidates (v0.3-rc4 tagged 2026-11-11).
items.uncertainty: LDK publishes git tags rather than GitHub releases; status is based on the tag and CHANGELOG.

disclaimer: Summaries are written in our own words and link to the original source. Merged is not released; released is not activated. Not investment advice.

inclusion_policy.critical_security: Include critical or security events even when existing status categories do not fit; require status_note explaining the exact branch/stage and mismatch. Never infer a tagged release or activation from a maintenance-branch merge.
